title: Jaani Khan and Maani Khan's Progeny Is Uprooted at Morinda

blocks.text: Inside Morinda, the fighting becomes intensely personal and punitive. The Singhs strike down the Ranghar leadership at close range, crushing many heads with hammers as they identify those held responsible for earlier crimes.

Among the names singled out above all others are Jaani Khan and Maani Khan, remembered here as the men who had handed over the Sahibzadas. The attack on their houses and heirs is narrated not as incidental battlefield killing, but as targeted vengeance against a known line of guilt.

The narrative presents that destruction as fulfillment rather than accident, treating Morinda’s punishment as falling on the line of Jaani Khan and Maani Khan. The Singhs are shown carrying out a sentence that the story had long prepared.
